hook: An FBI-submitted monochrome still image captured by a U.S. government sensor system, showing a small, dark, irregular object displaced slightly below and right of a central crosshair reticle, with swirling background patterns consistent with optical or infrared sensor imagery.
why_it_matters: This image represents a rare instance of the FBI formally submitting sensor imagery to AARO under the UAP reporting framework, indicating FBI operational systems are among the sensors capturing unexplained events. The redaction of the original imagery prior to AARO submission suggests classification concerns about either the sensor platform or the location — potentially limiting AARO's ability to conduct full analysis. The absence of a mission report and withheld date and location further constrain any resolution of what the object is.

key_findings.finding: The FBI was unable to identify the object observed in the imagery.
The source imagery was redacted before being submitted to AARO, and no accompanying mission report was provided, limiting the analytical record.
The image was derived from a U.S. government sensor system, suggesting the FBI operates or has access to technical collection platforms capable of capturing UAP events.
The object appears small, dark, and irregular in shape, positioned just off-center from the reticle, suggesting it was within the sensor's field of view but not the primary target.
No date or location metadata was provided with the submission, preventing temporal or geographic contextualization of the event.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The FBI submitted this image directly to AARO as part of the formal UAP reporting pipeline established under the UAP disclosure framework.

The imagery was derived from a U.S. government system and redacted prior to submission, which is consistent with protocols protecting national technical means, though no specific NRO attribution is made.
